- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commit 3eda79999f43373cda1d24fdab1a413072cca7b1
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Thu Jun 11 15:07:50 2026 +0800

    behavioral: ROI markers become RISC-V HINT NOPs (one ELF, every engine)
    
    Swap the marker encoding from csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 to the HINT pair
    slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 (enter) / 0x5A1 (exit). rd=x0 discards the result,
    so the markers execute as NOPs on every conforming core: the MILMB
    hazard is gone and a marker binary now runs standalone on --model fast
    and cycle AND drives --trigger marker on hybrid. SLTI has no compressed
    form, so the plugin's 4-byte gate and vsim's 16/32 scanner invariants
    hold unchanged.
    
    Dropped, not ported: the RUNTIME marker kind (csrw 0x7C0, rs1) -- it
    had no users outside its own unit tests. HandoffController loses the
    GprProbe parameter with it (vsim submodule 9521674).
    
    Users get markers from the runtime library: #include <andes_sim/roi.h>
    (andes_sim_roi_begin/end), installed to build/runtime/include/ and
    found through the same -B flag as the rest of the two-flag command.
    The MILMB warnings are deleted from the docs; vplat + markers compose.
    
    New acceptance test tests/vplat/test_vplat_markers.sh (RED before the

commit 3eda79999f43373cda1d24fdab1a413072cca7b1
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Thu Jun 11 15:07:50 2026 +0800

    behavioral: ROI markers become RISC-V HINT NOPs (one ELF, every engine)
    
    Swap the marker encoding from csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 to the HINT pair
    slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 (enter) / 0x5A1 (exit). rd=x0 discards the result,
    so the markers execute as NOPs on every conforming core: the MILMB
    hazard is gone and a marker binary now runs standalone on --model fast
    and cycle AND drives --trigger marker on hybrid. SLTI has no compressed
    form, so the plugin's 4-byte gate and vsim's 16/32 scanner invariants
    hold unchanged.
    
    Dropped, not ported: the RUNTIME marker kind (csrw 0x7C0, rs1) -- it
    had no users outside its own unit tests. HandoffController loses the
    GprProbe parameter with it (vsim submodule 9521674).
    
    Users get markers from the runtime library: #include <andes_sim/roi.h>
    (andes_sim_roi_begin/end), installed to build/runtime/include/ and
    found through the same -B flag as the rest of the two-flag command.
    The MILMB warnings are deleted from the docs; vplat + markers compose.
    
    New acceptance test tests/vplat/test_vplat_markers.sh (RED before the
    swap: fast standalone died in the MILMB trap loop). Validated: host
    doctests 4/4, full e2e 35/35 (marker/pc/neg), gemm 2/2, vplat 6/6,
    andes_sim 9/9 + f9, hsim kanata + kernel_cycles + test_small, parity.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Thu Jun 11 15:07:50 2026 +0800

    behavioral: ROI markers become RISC-V HINT NOPs (one ELF, every engine)
    
    Swap the marker encoding from csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 to the HINT pair
    slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 (enter) / 0x5A1 (exit). rd=x0 discards the result,
    so the markers execute as NOPs on every conforming core: the MILMB
    hazard is gone and a marker binary now runs standalone on --model fast
    and cycle AND drives --trigger marker on hybrid. SLTI has no compressed
    form, so the plugin's 4-byte gate and vsim's 16/32 scanner invariants
    hold unchanged.

    had no users outside its own unit tests. HandoffController loses the

    found through the same -B flag as the rest of the two-flag command.

+// 2-phase guard (L23 + L24): the writable M-mode CSRs round-trip across the
+// QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. A value stashed before the ROI is readable inside it
+// (ResumeDriver restores the CSR) and a value written inside the ROI is
+// captured at drain (StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough re-reads it).
 //
-// Phase A (QEMU1): write distinguishable values to mscratch, mtvec, and
-//                  mepc, then trigger the entry handoff.
-// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.  vsim does not modify these CSRs; they must
-//                  pass through the input-state snapshot kept by
-//                  HandoffController and arrive at QEMU 2 unchanged.
-// Phase C (QEMU2): csrr each CSR back into a GPR, compare. Exit code is
-//                  the CSR index of the first mismatch (1=mscratch,
-//                  2=mtvec, 3=mepc), 0 on full pass.
+// Covered CSRs:
+//   L23  mscratch                 -- M-mode software scratch (pure read/write)
+//   L24  mepc, mcause, mtval, mie -- writable trap/interrupt CSRs

-// mtvec is written with a 4-byte aligned value (mode=Direct) so QEMU
-// accepts it without rounding the low bits.

-#include "semihost_exit.inc"
+// History: this fixture predates the 2-phase redesign. It used to read the CSRs
+// back in a `phase_c` AFTER the exit marker and exit with the index of the
+// first mismatch -- but once the QEMU2 handback leg was removed, vsim drains and
+// exits AT the exit marker, so phase_c never ran and the guard was silently
+// dead. The check now lives INSIDE the ROI, where the vsim leg actually runs.
+//
+// Two assertion mechanisms:
+//   1. In-ROI self-check (works in the plain e2e harness, no --verify): read
+//      the CSR back inside the ROI and `bne` against the stashed sentinel,
+//      held in a callee-stable GPR which the GPR restore round-trips. On a
+//      regressed restore the values differ, so the fixture spins -- vsim never
+//      reaches the exit marker, times out, and the harness reports a failure.
+//      Used only for mscratch/mepc/mie, whose values round-trip exactly.
+//   2. --verify (VERIFY=1): the differential oracle compares the drained CSRs
+//      against a pure-QEMU run. Used for mcause (WLRL) and mtval (WARL), whose
+//      cross-engine legalisation could differ from a chosen sentinel; the
+//      oracle path compares engine-against-engine instead of against a literal.

+// Not asserted: mip (its pending bits are hardware-driven, not writable via
+// csrw on an M-only core) and the S-mode CSRs medeleg/mideleg/satp (the default
+// engine does not implement them). See docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \

builds an image from its `Dockerfile` (target `env`) and runs `./build.sh` inside.

## Running Tests

```sh
# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
bash scripts/run_e2e.sh

# Run with specific options
JOBS=4 MODE=csr bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, CSR-mode only
JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory

# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
# To run ctest directly after build:
#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
```

**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.

**Manual plugin tests**: `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` are QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests. They are run manually during plugin development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one leg, asserts on stdout).

## Architecture

### Two-Phase Handoff

```
QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
```

1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg (gdbstub P-packet restore into a freshly spawned QEMU) was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are not restored anywhere -- they remain in the struct as the drained record only. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

### Trigger Modes

- **CSR mode** (default): Pattern-matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (entry) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
- **PC mode**: ELF symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed.

Both modes coexist in the fixtures. `TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc` selects at runtime.

### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)

`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

## 2. Configuring the simulator

There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
vars in 2.1.

### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)

`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
somewhere non-default.

| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64` (external)    | every harness            |
| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*`                     | every harness            |
| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (some tests use 120)                        | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `csr`                                            | `csr` or `pc`            |
| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |

Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:

```sh
VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
  FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs bash tests/e2e.sh
```

`VSIM_BIN_DIR`); the commands in this section run THERE, not in this repo. Its
`config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The default is

If no mode arg is given, the default is CSR-insn match (M1): the

Example invocation (CSR mode, just the minimal arg):

```

### 2.4 vsim CLI flags

`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:

| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | M2 exit: drain when this PC retires.                    |
| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (e.g. OpenOCD).              |
| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |

Defaults for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the QEMU `virt` /
`andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.

Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
license-gated and off by default).

The shared mmaps created by the shell harnesses (`tests/e2e.sh`,
`tests/plugin/*.sh`) are hardcoded 128 MiB sparse
files under `/dev/shm` (`mktemp -p /dev/shm`).

## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use

| ID  | Trigger                                | Where        | When to pick it                                                |
|-----|----------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| M1  | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` insn match          | QEMU1 + vsim | Default. Your binary can embed `csrwi` markers.                |
| M2  | PC equals `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc`    | QEMU1 + vsim | Binary is yours, but you cannot insert CSR markers.            |

M1/M2 are the two ways to delimit the ROI. Every run ends at vsim's
exit-trigger drain.

Decision flow:

```
Can you edit the binary?
  yes -> insert csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 around the ROI -> M1
  no  -> resolve _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc symbols -> M2
```

> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (M1/M2):** keep the measured
> kernel anchored inside the `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` span -- read its inputs and
> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.

2) sim_ax45mpv_premium $ELF \

        --shared-mem-path $SHM --shared-mem-size 128MB

This document teaches one mode at a time.

### Quick map

| ID | Name                           | Drain trigger                                   | Used at        |
|----|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| M1 | CSR insn match (default)       | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (enter) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) | QEMU1, vsim    |
| M2 | PC symbol resolve              | PC equals `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc`   | QEMU1, vsim    |

M1/M2 are entry/exit triggers (the "boundary" question).
The vsim exit-trigger drain is the natural end-of-run signal.

---

## 1. One-time prerequisites

Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

### What it does

QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire
time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
same on `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes
ax45mp, so the fixture binary embeds these two `csrwi` instructions
at the ROI boundaries. vsim's exit drain (exit 200 + a non-empty
drained state file) is the end of the run.

### Inputs

- Fixture ELF with `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` in its source.
  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.

### Output

- Phase-by-phase log line + final `exit 0`.

### Run it

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=csr \
  bash tests/e2e.sh
```

Expected last line:

```
[rt_c_v_regs PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)

content.content:
[rt_c_v_regs PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)
```

### Drill-down (what the harness does internally)

The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the
M1 default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc`,
so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`
PCs at retire.

### Exercise 1

Switch fixture from `rt_c_v_regs` to `rt_c_matmul`. The script is
fixture-parameterized:

```sh
FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr \
  bash tests/e2e.sh
```

Verify the last line says `PASS] 2-phase handoff complete`. Then read
`tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.c` and confirm where the two
`csrwi 0x7C0, *` markers live (`enter_vsim()` / `exit_vsim()` helpers).

---

## 3. M2 - PC symbol resolve

### What it does

Same handoff as M1 but the trigger is a PC value (not an opcode
match). The harness runs `nm` on the ELF to resolve symbols
`_hybrid_enter_pc` and `_hybrid_exit_pc`, then passes:

- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)

CSR-mode matchers are bypassed; the `csrwi 0x7C0, *` instructions in
the binary become inert (CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor-defined write).

This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source.

### Inputs

- Same fixture as M1 (`rt_c_v_regs`), but the ELF must define
  `_hybrid_enter_pc` and `_hybrid_exit_pc` symbols. The C-level
  fixtures all do.

### Output

- `exit 0`, last log line `PASS] 2-phase handoff complete`.

### Run it

```sh
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=pc \
  bash tests/e2e.sh
```

### Drill-down

```sh
ENTER_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
              awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
EXIT_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
              awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')

# QEMU plugin arg
... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC

# vsim arg
... --hybrid-exit-pc 0x$EXIT_PC
```

### Exercise 2

Compare exit values: run the harness with TRIGGER_MODE=csr and again
with TRIGGER_MODE=pc on the same fixture. Both must exit 0 and
both must drain the same PC. Use:

```sh
xxd state_csr.bin | head -4
xxd state_pc.bin  | head -4
```

The PC field is at offset 16 (`hybrid_state_v1::pc`). For most
fixtures `pc(csr) == pc(pc)` because both modes drain right after
the entry trigger retires.

---

## 4. Running the whole suite

### Parallel runner (scripts/run_e2e.sh)

```sh
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

This runs every e2e fixture in both trigger modes (plus the negative
drivers) in parallel under a FIFO job pool.

> CAUTION: on this 128-core host the default `JOBS` value can saturate
> the box and time out. Use `JOBS=8` as a practical cap.

---

## 5. Switching-mode decision flow

When you have a new workload, pick a mode like this:

```
Is your binary YOURS to edit?
  yes -> Add csrwi 0x7C0, 0 and csrwi 0x7C0, 1 around the ROI -> M1
  no  -> Resolve _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc symbols -> M2
```

---

## 6. Common failure signatures

| Symptom                                                 | Likely cause                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `SKIP: ... not built`                                   | `source ./setup.sh` not run, or partial build                       |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                       | Trigger never fired (wrong mode, wrong PC)                          |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                     | Plugin hung -> `timeout` killed it; check the trigger choice        |
| `missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols`      | Wrong fixture for M2; rebuild with the symbols, or use M1 instead   |
| Whole suite times out under scripts/run_e2e.sh                  | `JOBS` too high; set `JOBS=8`                                       |

---

## 7. Review checklist (for the reviewer)

Use this when sanity-checking the tutorial against the code:

- [ ] Plugin arg names match `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`
      (`outfile`, `enter_pc`).
- [ ] vsim flag names match `verilator/src/main.cpp`
      (`--resume-from-qemu`, `--handoff-out`, `--hybrid-exit-pc`,
      `--shared-mem-{path,size,base}`).
- [ ] `scripts/run_e2e.sh` runs every fixture in both csr and pc modes.

content.content:
1. **Memory is shared, not copied.** Both simulators `mmap` the same backing file (`/dev/shm/...`) as their RAM. When QEMU writes a byte at `0x80001000`, vsim sees it instantly, and vice versa. RAM size becomes irrelevant. 2. **All architectural state fits in one packed struct.** GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, mtvec, ...), PMP (16 cfg + 64 addr), V scalar CSRs (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, vlenb), and the full V regfile (`v0..v31`, up to 2 KB) all live in `struct hybrid_state_v1` (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). That struct is the wire contract every component agrees on. 3. **vsim only refreshes what the ROI can mutate.** vsim restores into the hart only what it needs to run (GPRs + PC + V state); on the way out it drains back only what could have changed (GPRs + PC + V state). Everything else (FP, M-mode CSRs, PMP, V regfile bytes when the ROI doesn't touch them) **passes through unchanged** from the QEMU 1 snapshot into the drained output file. This skips ~85+ DMI transactions per handoff. 4. **The trigger is a magic CSR write or a PC match.** `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` enters vsim; `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` exits it. CSR `0x7C0` is in the user-defined range. A third form, `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1`, decides at runtime based on `rs1`'s value (1 = exit). PC-trigger mode skips the magic CSR entirely - the harness names entry/exit PCs on the CLI. 5. **Microarchitectural state is thrown away.** Caches, TLB, branch predictor, store buffer - none of it transfers. We accept cold caches at handoff and rely on a "warm-up window" before recording. ## State Categories and Their Transport The wire struct is uniform; transport per category depends on what QEMU's plugin API and the AX45MPV Debug Module are willing to expose. | Category | QEMU 1 -> snapshot | snapshot -> vsim hart | vsim hart -> snapshot | |---------------------------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------| | GPRs `x1..x31`, PC | TCG plugin reads | DM Abstract Commands (DPC for PC) | DM Abstract Commands (fresh read) | | `mtvec` | TCG plugin | DM Abstract Command | passthrough (not re-read) | | Other M-mode CSRs (`mstatus`, `mepc`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `mcycle`, `minstret`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `satp`) | TCG plugin | passthrough (not written) | passthrough | | FPRs `f0..f31` | TCG plugin | passthrough | passthrough | | PMP (16 cfg + 64 addr) | TCG plugin | passthrough | passthrough | | V scalar CSRs - `vtype`, `vl` | TCG plugin | DM Program Buffer running `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` | DM Abstract Command (fresh read) | | V scalar CSRs - `vstart`, `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`, `mstatus.VS` | TCG plugin | DM Abstract Command, **with Program-Buffer fallback** if the DM rejects | DM Abstract Command (fresh read) | | V regfile `v0..v31` (up to 2 KB) | TCG plugin | shared-mmap scratch region (`hybrid::kVScratchGpa = 0x80FF0000`); fixture executes `vle8.v` to load | fixture executes `vse8.v` back to scratch; vsim memcpys those bytes into `state.vreg[]` | | `vlenb` | TCG plugin | not restored (read-only, fixed by NDS_VLEN) | passthrough (verified, not re-read) | | Guest memory | -- (in shared mmap) | -- (in shared mmap) | -- (in shared mmap) | "Passthrough" means: vsim copies the field from the inbound snapshot into the outbound snapshot unchanged. The hart never sees it; the field rides from QEMU 1 straight into the drained output file. ## Trigger Modes Two ways to delimit the ROI; pick at runtime via `TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc`. | Mode | Entry into vsim | Exit out of vsim | Source of truth | |------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------| | CSR | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (or `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` with `rs1==0`) | `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (or `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` with `rs1==1`) | the binary itself | | PC | plugin arg `enter_pc=0x...` (no insn match) | vsim CLI `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x...` (synthetic hit added via `CsrTrigger::add_pc_hit`) | the harness/CLI; binary is unchanged | Three handoff kinds (`hybrid_handoff_kind` in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h`): - `HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER` - QEMU drains and exits; vsim ignores at retire. subgraph QEMU1["QEMU 1 (functional, MHz)"] Q1_TCG["TCG insn loop"] Q1_PLUGIN["hybrid_handoff.so
CSR mode: csrwi 0x7C0,0
PC mode: enter_pc=0x..."] Q1_TCG --> Q1_PLUGIN end subgraph VSIM["vsim (cycle-accurate, KHz)"] V_PIPE["RTL pipeline
(Verilator + SystemC)"] V_DM["JTAG DM driver (in-process)
Abstract Cmds + Program Buffer"] V_TRIG["CsrTrigger
CSR mode: csrwi 0x7C0,1 (or runtime form)
PC mode: --hybrid-exit-pc"] V_CTRL["HandoffController
passthrough(snapshot) +
fresh GPR/PC/V-CSR drain"] V_DM -.GPR/FPR/CSR + vsetvl.-> V_PIPE V_PIPE -.retire signals.-> V_TRIG V_TRIG --> V_CTRL V_CTRL --> V_DM end ``` Phase 1 (QEMU 1) Phase 2 (vsim) ----------------- --------------------------------- seed[0..15] = pattern vle32.v v8..v15, (seed) csrwi 0x7C0, 0 vadd.vi v9, v9, +100 store result row to .bss (anchor) vse8.v v0..v31, (V_SCRATCH) csrwi 0x7C0, 1 <- run ends here ``` (The old Phase 3 - a QEMU 2 that stored and verified the result - was removed with the QEMU2 leg. The mutated V state now lands in the drained state file.) ### State that crosses each handoff | vsim | TRAPS (newlib stdio -> `_write` -> semihosting ebreak -> `mtvec`) | not implemented -> trap loop | **register / memory only**. No `printf`, no syscalls, no `_exit`. | The runtime (`rt_c_helpers.h`) marks the boundary: ```c // ===== QEMU 1 window ===== // printf etc. are fine enter_vsim(); // csrwi 0x7C0, 0 -> hand off to vsim // ===== vsim window ===== // syscall-free: registers + memory only exit_vsim(); // csrwi 0x7C0, 1 -> vsim drains; run ends // (code after the exit marker never executes in a hybrid run) ``` The forbidden-ness in phase 2 is transitive: anything that ultimately calls `_write`/`_exit`/`_open`/... (i.e. anything that emits via the libgloss syscall stubs) is out. Pure CPU functions are fine: `vsnprintf` into a buffer, `memcpy`, ``, inline asm including V instructions, `setjmp`/`longjmp`. The pattern for cross-phase output is "emit in phase 1, compute in phase 2, and let the drained state file carry the results out." **Plan the phase your I/O goes in.** ### 2. Only GPRs / PC / V-state survive vsim mutation vsim refreshes only `x1..x31` + PC + (when V is enabled) the six V CSRs out of the hart at the exit trigger. Everything else - **FPRs, M-mode CSRs except `mtvec`, PMP, `vlenb`** - rides along untouched in QEMU 1's snapshot. Concretely: - Mutating `f3` inside vsim: the drained state file holds QEMU 1's value of `f3`. Silently lost. - Mutating `mscratch`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`, ... inside vsim: silently lost. - Mutating PMP inside vsim: silently lost. - Mutating `mtvec`: lost (vsim writes its own mtvec back in but doesn't drain it; the snapshot wins). If your test depends on observing a non-GPR mutation after the run, route it through memory instead: store the value to a known address inside the ROI and inspect the shared mmap afterwards. ### 3. The V regfile only round-trips if the fixture cooperates `v0..v31` doesn't ride DM Abstract Commands. Vsim memcpys QEMU 1's `state.vreg[]` into a fixed scratch region (`V_SCRATCH = 0x80FF0000`, 2 KB) on resume; the fixture's vsim-phase prologue must `vle8.v v0..v31, (V_SCRATCH)` to load those bytes into the real regfile. Drain mirrors: the fixture's vsim-phase epilogue must `vse8.v v0..v31, (V_SCRATCH)` before the exit trigger, otherwise `state.vreg[]` lands in the drained state file with stale (or zero) bytes. `rt_c_v_regs.c` is the worked example. ### 4. `mstatus.VS` (and `.FS`) must already be set when QEMU 1 drains ResumeDriver writes `mstatus` to the vsim hart **only** if the QEMU 1 snapshot has VS bits non-zero (`state.mstatus & 0x600u`). The shared `runtime/crt0.S` runs before the QEMU 1 drain marker and sets `mstatus.VS=Initial` and `mstatus.FS=Initial`. **If you skip the standard crt0**, set both yourself before `csrwi 0x7C0, 0`. Otherwise vsim resumes with `VS=Off` and the very first `vsetvli` in your ROI raises illegal-insn -> trap loop. ### 5. The trigger instruction must be 4-byte `csrwi` The plugin filters on a 32-bit insn (`size != 4` is rejected). Don't let the assembler emit a compressed form. The runtime helpers wrap the asm in inline strings; if you write the trigger by hand, force `.option norvc` around it. ### 6. Stay inside the shared 128 MB RAM window Default mmap window: `0x80000000..0x88000000` (QEMU virt's RAM base + 128 MB). The runtime puts: - `.text/.rodata/.data/.bss` at `0x80000000` upward (`runtime/rt_c.ld`).

3	// Tier-1 fixture: M-mode CSRs survive QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2.
4	// Verifies the CSR pass-through merge in HandoffController and the
5	// feature-aware P-packet path in qemu_handback.

7	// Phase A (QEMU1): write distinguishable values to mscratch, mtvec, and
8	//                  mepc, then trigger the entry handoff.
9	// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.  vsim does not modify these CSRs; they must
10	//                  pass through the input-state snapshot kept by
11	//                  HandoffController and arrive at QEMU 2 unchanged.
12	// Phase C (QEMU2): csrr each CSR back into a GPR, compare. Exit code is
13	//                  the CSR index of the first mismatch (1=mscratch,
14	//                  2=mtvec, 3=mepc), 0 on full pass.
15	//
16	// mtvec is written with a 4-byte aligned value (mode=Direct) so QEMU

1	/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
2	 *
3	 * Phase rule:
4	 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
5	 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
6	 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
7	 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
8	 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
9	 *   to register/memory work only.
10	 *
11	 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) via standard
12	 *   newlib stdio; the QEMU launch sets -semihosting-config
13	 *   enable=on,target=native. The hybrid run ENDS at the vsim drain on
14	 *   exit_vsim (there is no QEMU2 leg), so code after the exit marker
15	 *   never executes in a hybrid run.
16	 */
17	
18	#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
19	#define RT_C_HELPERS_H
20	
21	/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
22	 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
23	 *
24	 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
25	 * with the csrwi insn. The labels are inert in CSR mode and consumed by
26	 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
27	 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
28	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
29	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
30	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
31	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
32	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
33	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
34	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
35	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
36	/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
37	 *
38	 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
39	 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
40	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
41	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
42	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
43	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
44	 * consumes the value.)
45	 *
46	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
47	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
48	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
49	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
50	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
51	 *     between the markers.
52	 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
53	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
54	 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
55	 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
56	 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
57	 * attribution. */
58	static inline void enter_vsim(void)
59	{
60	  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_enter_pc\n"
61	                       "_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
62	                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
63	}
64	static inline void exit_vsim(void)
65	{
66	  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
67	                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
68	                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
69	}
70	
71	#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: objdump not found at $OBJDUMP"
      exit 77
    fi
    # Derive the two switch PCs from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs, scanning
    # `objdump -d` raw bytes: ENTER = the entry marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`
    # (encoding 5a002013), EXIT = the LAST exit marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`
    # (encoding 5a102013). Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin
    # (enter_pc=) and vsim (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the
    # trigger (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC
    # reproduces marker mode's switch points exactly. EXIT keeps the LAST
    # marker so a fixture that jumps over poison exit-marker padding
    # (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first dead
    # one. So pc mode needs no per-fixture config and no planted boundary
    # symbols.
    MARKERS=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '
      $2 == "5a002013" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
      $2 == "5a102013"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
      END {
        if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
        else                              { exit 1 }
      }') || {
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE pc]: could not derive ROI marker PCs from $VSIM_ELF"
      exit 1
    }
    ENTER_PC="${MARKERS%% *}"
    EXIT_PC="${MARKERS##* }"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are not restored anywhere -- they remain in the struct as the drained record only. ## 0. The one-paragraph mental model

QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write or PC)
hands control between them. One run is two legs:

```
   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate; run ends here)
Run a subset:

```sh
FILTER=rt_c_v JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh        # only V-related fixtures
MODE=csr     JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # skip the pc-mode iterations
JOBS=1                     bash scripts/run_e2e.sh  # sequential for debugging
LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs       bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

---

## 6. Common failures and how to read them

| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC.                          |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                    | `timeout` killed the plugin. Increase `TIMEOUT` or tune the target.  |
| `missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols`     | M2 needs a fixture with those labels. Rebuild or use M1.             |
| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

---

# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises

Status: draft for review
Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
Scope: every switching mode (M1, M2) the repo ships, with copy-paste
commands and one exercise per mode.

---

## 0. What "switching mode" means

The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:

```
   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate; run ends here)
```

A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN each leg drains its
state and hands off. The codebase ships two rules (M1, M2). They
plug into the same harness; you pick the rule with plugin args and
vsim CLI flags. The fixture binary does NOT need to change between
rules (one fixture can be driven by several modes). Every run ends at
vsim's exit-trigger drain; there is no QEMU2 leg.
| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`        | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
| `tests/fixtures/*.elf`           | Test fixtures (e.g. rt_c_v_regs)  |

Common env vars (auto-detected by the harness; override only if you
keep these elsewhere):

```sh
export VSIM_QEMU=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
export VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
export VSIM_BIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
```

content.content:
## Trigger Modes

Two ways to delimit the ROI; pick at runtime via `TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc`.

| Mode | Entry into vsim                                | Exit out of vsim                              | Source of truth |
|------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| CSR  | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (or `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` with `rs1==0`) | `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (or `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` with `rs1==1`) | the binary itself |
| PC   | plugin arg `enter_pc=0x...` (no insn match)    | vsim CLI `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x...` (synthetic hit added via `CsrTrigger::add_pc_hit`) | the harness/CLI; binary is unchanged |

Three handoff kinds (`hybrid_handoff_kind` in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h`):

- `HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER` - QEMU drains and exits; vsim ignores at retire.
- `HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT`  - vsim drains and exits (the end of the run); QEMU does not encounter this PC.
- `HYBRID_HANDOFF_RUNTIME` - vsim decodes `rs1` from the matched insn, reads its current GPR value, fires only when it equals 1. Lets a single binary parameterize entry vs exit at runtime.

## Design Rationale

**One packed struct is the wire format.** Two components in two languages (QEMU plugin in C, vsim in C++) need to agree byte-for-byte on what state means. A C struct in a shared header (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) is the simplest contract that compiles into both. Versioning is via `magic` + `version`, with `reserved` bytes for forward growth (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr were added by consuming `reserved` rather than bumping to v2).

ResumeDriver writes `mstatus` to the vsim hart **only** if the QEMU 1 snapshot has VS bits non-zero (`state.mstatus & 0x600u`). The shared `runtime/crt0.S` runs before the QEMU 1 drain marker and sets `mstatus.VS=Initial` and `mstatus.FS=Initial`. **If you skip the standard crt0**, set both yourself before `csrwi 0x7C0, 0`. Otherwise vsim resumes with `VS=Off` and the very first `vsetvli` in your ROI raises illegal-insn -> trap loop.

### 5. The trigger instruction must be 4-byte `csrwi`

The plugin filters on a 32-bit insn (`size != 4` is rejected). Don't let the assembler emit a compressed form. The runtime helpers wrap the asm in inline strings; if you write the trigger by hand, force `.option norvc` around it.

### 6. Stay inside the shared 128 MB RAM window

### Where each rule lives in the runtime

| Concern                                         | File                                           |
|-------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Memory map (`_stack`, `_end`, load address)       | `runtime/rt_c.ld`                              |
| `mstatus.{FS,VS}` init, sp/gp, `.bss` clear       | `runtime/crt0.S`                               |
| M-mode trap save/restore + fatal trap reporter    | `runtime/trap.S` + `runtime/handler.c`         |
| Newlib syscall stubs (`_write`/`_exit`/`_sbrk`/...) via semihosting | `-lgloss_vh` from the Andes toolchain |
| Phase markers (`enter_vsim`, `exit_vsim`)         | `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`                       |
| `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` labels for PC-trigger mode | `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h` (resolved by `scripts/run_e2e.sh` via `nm`) |
| QEMU launch flags (`-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`, `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`) | `tests/e2e.sh` (QEMU 1) |
| C-fixture build line (`-nodefaultlibs -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc`) | `tests/fixtures/Makefile` |

For pure-asm fixtures (`handoff_roundtrip.S`, `rt_all_gprs.S`, ...) the runtime is skipped entirely: link with `handoff_roundtrip.ld` and inline `semihost_exit.inc` for a standalone (non-hybrid) exit path. Rules 1, 2, 4-7 still apply; you just hand-code the same checks instead of relying on `runtime/`.

## Known Limitations

cd /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim && git add -u && git status --short && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(plugin): ROI markers become RISC-V HINT NOPs; triggers are marker|pc

The magic trigger drops the `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` encoding for the HINT
pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (enter) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit): rd=x0
discards the result, so the markers execute as architectural NOPs and
one marked ELF runs on every engine and on real silicon -- CSR 0x7C0 is
MILMB on Andes cores, so the old exit marker enabled ILM at base 0 and
wedged standalone runs. SLTI has no compressed form, so the plugin's
4-byte insn gate stays exact; the unused RUNTIME kind (`csrw 0x7C0,
rs1`) is dropped, not ported. The mode named after the retired
mechanism dies with it: trigger modes are marker (default) and pc
across the plugin, the harness (TRIGGER_MODE/MODE values in
tests/e2e.sh and scripts/run_e2e.sh), and the docs. The fixtures'
planted `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` labels go too: pc mode now derives
both switch PCs from the marker encodings via objdump (first 5a002013
= enter, LAST 5a102013 = exit, so rt_pc_jump's poison exit padding
resolves to the real, reachable exit). Validated: the plugin and all
fixtures rebuild, the QEMU1 leg drains with rc=200 in both marker and
pc mode, and a marked binary runs standalone to its semihosting exit
(rc=3) where the csrwi encoding used to hang.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
